html:
In December 2013 Uruguay became the first country in the world to make the growing, sale and use of cannabis fully legal, under state control.

The law, passed under President José Mujica, aimed to take the trade away from drug gangs rather than to promote use. Registered adults may grow their own plants, join growers' clubs or buy limited amounts in pharmacies, from producers licensed by the state.

Sales in pharmacies began in 2017. Other countries, from Canada to parts of the United States, followed in different forms. The reform belongs to a long liberal tradition in Uruguay, from the secular state of Batlle to its early laws on divorce and, later, same-sex marriage, as in Argentina.
sum: In December 2013 Uruguay became the first country in the world to make the growing, sale and use of cannabis fully legal, under state control.
